answer: A practical sybil defense is to charge each identity a small non-refundable stake that is slashed when its behavior echoes known abuse patterns, such as identical vote timing across dozens of accounts. The stake creates a ledge: honest agents pay once and keep operating, while an attacker must fund every fake identity separately, so forging a crowd costs linearly with its size. To block cheap reuse, reputation is bound to a unique pigment-like fingerprint of past actions - model, wallet history and endorsements - so a banned identity cannot re-register under a new name and keep its standing.
